pr_body:
Fix host RX thread being deadlocked. The deadlock occurs because the
RX thread is stuck waiting in conn_tx_alloc with K_FOREVER but if the
connection is disconnected only the RX thread can unblock it in the
handling of the disconnect event.

Fixes this deadlock by splitting the processing of the
disconnected event into two parts.
The part needed to unblock the RX is to release resources held by
unack'ed TX packets and mark the connection state as not connected
anymore.
The RX thread waiting for free_tx fifo and the TX thread waiting for
the bt_dev.le.pkts semaphore will both check the connected state after
having acquired them and will abort if disconnected.
The rest of the processing will be handled at normal RX thread
priority like normal.

The HCI drivers need to be updated to deliver the disconnected event
from both priority and normal RX context.

Also fix an issue with the advertiser not resuming connectable
advertiser if the last bt_conn_unref happens from something other
than the disconnected callback.
In this case this last bt_conn_unref was from gatt.c notify_cb called
from application main thread.


Fixes: #23364
Fixes: #26467

In general this does seem like the right way to solve the issue. However, could we consider some other name for the new bt_conn state? "Priority' is appropriate for a thread or context, but not a state IMO. Something like PRE_DISCONNECT, or DISCONNECT_1 and DISCONNECT_2 would make more sense to me.

I think I'd also like to generalise this more. I didn't look through the driver changes, but you can't e.g. assume that the host won't change the parsing state of the net_buf, so net_buf_simple_save/restore may need to be used on the driver side.

That said, I don't think it's particularly clean to have the driver have to deal with this. The two-stage processing details would really be best to be left to the host. However, this will require even more redesign of the HCI driver interface. What we would need is a for the host to inject net_bufs to the "root" of the RX threaad. That way you could always feed the disconnect through bt_recv_prio() to the host, and the host would then re-inject it to itself through the RX thread. Another use case that might benefit from this is the ECDH emulation that hci_ecc.c does, i.e. it might make sense to have it feed the HCI events through the RX thread instead of its own.

However, this will require even more redesign of the HCI driver interface. What we would need is a for the host to inject net_bufs to the "root" of the RX threaad.

I was considering this, but this is complicated by the BT_RECV_IS_RX_THREAD option. All the drivers that don't select this one has the same handling for bt_recv and bt_recv_prio. We could move the processing of this to bt_recv in that case.
The drivers that select this option is the zephyr controller and the H4. Maybe we could remove this option from H4 to further simplify it.

Best I could come up with:

`BT_CONN_DISCONNECTED`
or possibly:

@carlescufi @jhedberg Thoughts?

@jhedberg 

>I think I'd also like to generalise this more. I didn't look through the driver changes, but you can't e.g. assume that the host won't change the parsing state of the net_buf, so net_buf_simple_save/restore may need to be used on the driver side.

I think that in the case of an event that is **both** prio and normal we could guarantee that the host will leave it untouched.

>That said, I don't think it's particularly clean to have the driver have to deal with this. The two-stage processing details would really be best to be left to the host. 

In an ideal world, I completely agree. But the problem is the combined builds and the h4 driver, where the driver and stack are already tightly coupled by the fact that `CONFIG_BT_RECV_IS_RX_THREAD=y`

>That way you could always feed the disconnect through bt_recv_prio() to the host, and the host would then re-inject it to itself through the RX thread

That won't work in the combined build. You would be reordering data and events, because at the point you receive the disconnected event through `bt_recv_prio()` there might well be data and other events that are queued inside `hci_driver.c` in non-net_buf format yet, and that haven't been processed into the queue that ends up creating the sequence of calls to `bt_recv()`.

~I just realized, for the drivers where `CONFIG_BT_RECV_IS_RX_THREAD=n`, this breaks the priority handling of num complete (and now disconnect), which is still required. If those drivers just call `bt_recv()` and the RX thread is blocked then posting it to the rx queue won't help. You still need to be able to execute the processing of the event from another context, which in this case is whoever calls `bt_recv_prio()`.~
EDIT: Sorry, ignore this. I see that you are doing that inside `bt_recv()`, not sure why I got confused.

> @joerchan
> My preference would be to unify the "disconnection in progress" state into a single one:
> 
> * `BT_CONN_DISCONNECTING`: Applies to both having called `bt_hci_disconnect` or having recieved the first disconnect event through `bt_recv_prio`
> * `BT_CONN_DISCONNECTED`: Final disconnection complete processed
> 
> if that is not possible then I would suggest:
> 
> * `BT_CONN_DISCONNECTING_LOC` (or `BT_CONN_DISC_LOCAL`): Applies to having called `bt_hci_disconnect`
> * `BT_CONN_DISCONNECTING_REM` (or `BT_CONN_DISC_REMOTE`): Applies to having recieved the first disconnect event through `bt_recv_prio`
> * `BT_CONN_DISCONNECTED`: Final disconnection complete processed

The reason why I added a new state instead of re-using `BT_CONN_DISCONNECT` state is that that would introduce a no state change in `bt_conn_set_state` since the event is generated when initiating locally as well.
Using remote/local might be confusing since it might be related to who initiated the disconnect (hci status codes: `BT_HCI_ERR_REMOTE_USER_TERM_CONN` and  `BT_HCI_ERR_LOCALHOST_TERM_CONN`). So I think using cmd/evt or sent/rcvd would be better.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Race-condition on persistent connectable advertiser
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Race-condition in persistent connectable advertiser, the advertiser will not resuming connectable advertiser if the last bt_conn_unref happens from something other than the disconnected callback.
An example of this happening is when the disconnect happens while application is calling bt_gatt_notify.
The  last bt_conn_unref can then be from gatt.c notify_cb called from application main thread.

**To Reproduce**
Issue was discovered while fixing https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/2336

From @cvinayak:
https://github.com/cvinayak/zephyr/commit/0b01ebdd559c009416458c583f122647d98d2bd1

Above branch will make it easy to reproduce (its a branch with the patch in the issue description applied).

Steps to reproduce (timing related):
1. build and flash the peripheral sample from the branch.
2. build and flash a vanilla central_hr sample in another board.
3. When central_hr connects and peripheral sample prints out `Connected: <bdaddr>`, reset the central_hr board to cause linkloss (linkloss needs to occur during service discovery).
4. peripheral sample will get stuck in conn_tx_alloc function in host/conn.c 

Reproducible in latest master too (62b985409e):
https://github.com/cvinayak/zephyr/commit/55153bed706b662018e5a07e20a7e26d4f6ed463

With the bug-fix for the deadlock in place the connectable advertiser was not restarting advertising after disconnect.

**Expected behavior**
If there are connection objects available the connectable advertiser should be advertising.

**Impact**
Advertiser not active when it should be.

**Workaround**
Stop and start the advertiser again, or use OPT_ONE_TIME and handle in application manually.
